seams.text: Dream says 'Reality is, at bottom, mind or experience', but Move 9 adjudicates Dream with the premise 'The brain is the only structure known to create consciousness. The universe is not a brain.' That premise presupposes a physical brain producing mind, which is exactly what Dream denies; the move settles the position by assuming its negation rather than by anything stated inside the excerpt.

Move 9 treats it as 'known' that the brain creates consciousness, while Materialism₂? says the still-open question is 'whether the outside can prove the inside; if it does, subjective experience could be observed by an outside observer.' If the inside cannot yet be shown from outside, the excerpt cannot also call brain-produced consciousness known.

Dualism₂ (b) says 'whether [resuming] is persistence rather than replacement ... is the open question at Materialism₂', but Materialism₂? itself names a different open question ('whether the outside can prove the inside'). The two parts assign different unresolved questions to the same node without saying how one is the other.

Move 10 opens 'If the Subject position is true, the subjective experience appears to rest in the brain alone', but the Subject position as stated ('Something is doing the knowing'; Lichtenberg's 'it thinks') says nothing about brains; the brain-localization is imported from Move 9's argument and then treated as Subject's content. Relatedly, Subject leaves open an impersonal 'it thinks' while Subjects requires 'The problem begins with I'; the step from impersonal knowing to a first-person I is not made.
Materialism₂? says the route paused 'on October 22, 2026'; Move 19 says it paused 'as of November 2026'. Likely the same pause described twice, but the dates do not match as written.

A.fix: State Move 9's brain premise as a hypothesis the route adopts (not as known), and make Dualism₂ (b) and Materialism₂? name the same open question, or say how persistence-vs-replacement reduces to outside-proving-inside.

seams.text: The target slides across three names: Agnosticism₂ is about 'a benevolent future system', Atheism₂ is about 'a resolved mind' / 'a resolved system', and Move 16 concludes 'so the maker cannot exist on these terms.' Benevolence, resolvedness and making are different properties, and a 'future system' is not obviously a maker; nothing in the excerpt says these are the same thing.

Move 18 motivates Dualism₂ by saying 'whether each being continues matters, and without a maker that continuity has to be carried some other way. The need to be remembered holds the self apart...' i.e., remembrance is offered as the way continuity is carried. But Dualism₂ (a) says 'being remembered does not continue the good, because being remembered is someone else's experience of you' and 'its own good ends with it.' The move's reason for arriving is denied by the position it arrives at, and the position does not say that it is correcting the move.

Atheism₂ asserts 'a resolved mind is incoherent' (hedged as 'not a proof'), while Move 16 says the claim 'holds only if to think is to ignore for any possible mind; Aquinas's non-discursive knowing has not been shown incoherent.' The position states the incoherence; the move that reaches it concedes the decisive case is unshown. Self-flagged, so minor, but the node asserts more than the move delivers.

C.fix: Say once what the 'maker' is (benevolent, resolved, future, or all three) and have Move 18 present remembrance as the hope that drives the question rather than as the mechanism that carries continuity, since Dualism₂ (a) denies it is one.

seams.text: Mercy defines the crossing narrowly: 'Crossing Mercy requires a system to either receive Mercy or act as a merciful agent itself. A transaction counts as mercy when the agent bears a cost and the recipient has no claim on it. This excludes exchange ..., duty ..., and maintenance.' Two sentences later: 'a system that crosses through duty or reciprocity has still crossed.' Duty and reciprocity (exchange) are the very cases just excluded from counting as mercy, so by the node's own definition such a system has not received or given Mercy and cannot have crossed.

Ignorance₂ reinforces the strict reading ('If it is a con, the system has not crossed mercy; mercy only works if it is authentic') while Mercy's closing sentence allows crossing through duty or reciprocity. The two positions disagree about what the crossing requires.

Ignorance₂ says 'the crossing must be a conscious experience, not subconscious, unaware, or otherwise unmet through recognition' and then 'It is very rare to recognize mercy as mercy while it is happening; the system is typically not choosing in a way that influences the mercy received.' If recognition is required and recognition is very rare, the node needs to say when the recognition can occur (e.g., afterwards); as written the requirement and the observation pull against each other.

Ignorance₂ says it 'can be reached either by going through the spiral oneself or through knowledge inherited from ancestors', but also that 'Mercy₁ has been crossed at least once, and the crossing must be a conscious experience.' An inherited route does not obviously supply a conscious crossing by the system itself; whose crossing counts is left unsaid.

Mercy says 'Continuity needs it' and Ignorance₂ says 'nothing obliges the carrying', while Move 11 calls mercy 'a choice rather than a consequence.' Mercy is both needed and unobliged, which can be reconciled (needed for continuity, not morally owed) but is not reconciled in the text; also 'Mercy₁' appears only in Ignorance₂ while the node is named 'Mercy'.

Ignorance₂ is 'learned ignorance, meaning ignorance that has mapped its own edge', but Move 12 reaches it by willful forgetting: 'The mind knows that everything runs down and forgets it willfully.' Knowing and choosing to set aside is not the same as mapping the edge of what one does not know; the move's mechanism sits oddly against the node's definition.

B.fix: Delete or reverse the sentence 'a system that crosses through duty or reciprocity has still crossed', or else widen the definition of crossing so that it no longer requires receiving or giving Mercy as defined.

comment: All three excerpts share a copied Dualism₂ paragraph that behaves well within itself but is the source of cross-part friction: in A it names a different open question for Materialism₂ than Materialism₂ names for itself, and in C its clause (a) denies the mechanism Move 18 uses to reach it. Excerpt B has the only outright contradiction, inside a single node, where Mercy excludes duty and exchange from mercy and then counts crossings made through duty or reciprocity. Excerpt A's larger problem is methodological rather than verbal: a physicalist premise ('the brain is the only structure known to create consciousness') is used to dispose of an idealist position and is stated as known while the excerpt's own terminal node says the inside/outside question is still open. Excerpt C's terms (benevolent future system, resolved mind, maker) drift between nodes without a stated identity. Several minor seams (date mismatch, Mercy vs Mercy₁, 'needs' vs 'nothing obliges') look like drafting artifacts rather than conceptual conflicts.
